strengths: The connection between unbounded forest/network partitions and overconfident extrapolation motivates an understandable density-based remedy. This is relevant to researchers studying uncertainty estimation and OOD detection.

The five controlled simulations evaluate classification error, posterior estimation, and OOD detection. Figure 2 reports 45 repetitions with interquartile ranges, and Table 1 shows substantial improvements over the corresponding parent models.

The shared framework for forests and networks, explicit mixture construction, and pseudocode communicate the main idea clearly. The supplied results offer a useful proof of concept, particularly for balanced, two-dimensional problems.
weaknesses: Necessary: Correct the central uniform-confidence claim. For fixed training data and positive delta, Equations (3.6)–(3.8) imply that the posterior approaches the empirical class prior as Gaussian densities vanish. It approaches 1/K only when those priors are uniform. The balanced experiments conceal this discrepancy with Equation (2.1). Either restrict the claim explicitly or modify and validate the construction.

Necessary: Support or narrow the theoretical claims. Section 1 asserts convergence to the true distribution without a theorem, assumptions, or conditions governing partitions, neighborhood bandwidths, and covariance estimates. Moreover, Gaussian tail decay establishes behavior sufficiently far from the fitted components; it does not establish uniform confidence everywhere outside the distribution's support. The exterior-square experiments provide limited evidence for the much broader problem formulated in Section 2.1.

Necessary: Resolve the KDN specification mismatch. Equation (3.4) compares pre-activations, whereas Algorithm 3 accumulates differences between post-activations. These define different weights: with one hidden layer, Equation (3.4) is identically zero because first-layer pre-activations are globally affine, while Algorithm 3 can distinguish activation regions. State which construction produced the results. Also specify how singular covariance estimates are handled when too few positively weighted samples support a kernel.

Necessary: Supply essential experimental details. Values and selection procedures for C, h, and T are absent, although they control the tradeoff between confidence on training-distribution inputs and OOD inputs. Specify independent training/evaluation sampling, network stopping rules, the OOD sampling distribution, and the score and positive-class convention used for AUROC/FPR@95. Correct the Gaussian XOR definition, which currently gives identical class-conditional means, and explain truncation and the reference posteriors used for Hellinger distance. These omissions prevent reliable reproduction and assessment of the claimed use of only in-distribution data.

Necessary: Reconcile the conclusions with Figure 2. The statement that posterior estimates are 'always' closer to the truth is contradicted by the larger KDF/KDN Hellinger errors on Gaussian XOR at small sample sizes. KDF also has substantially worse small-sample classification error on Circle. Replace the unconditional 'without sacrificing any in-distribution performance' claim with a description of the observed dependence on dataset and sample size.

Necessary: Reanalyse or narrow the human-study interpretation. Figure 3 averages class probabilities across responses. An average near 0.5 can arise from equally many confident predictions for opposite classes, so it does not establish individual uncertainty. To support that interpretation, report response-level confidence or entropy with participant-level uncertainty estimates. Explain the choice of the 82-degree slice and report the second task, or limit the conclusion to the displayed aggregate responses rather than general properties of human intelligence.

Optional: Compare against a conventional KDE or Gaussian mixture with the same additive floor, and ablate neighborhood weighting. These controls would clarify what the learned partitions contribute beyond generic density decay. Larger figure labels and runtime/memory measurements would also improve usability.
